title: Tell the planner to deliver the plan inside the JSON contract object
rationale: The role prompt never states how the result must be delivered; the contract schema only arrives appended to the task message, and the closing instruction ('Before returning the plan…') invites a prose answer. Stating the delivery form in the role prompt removes an entire duplicated plan-generation turn on every run where the model writes prose.
evidence: events.jsonl:7058 `contract_invalid agent=planner attempt=0 errors=["no JSON object found in final assistant message"]`; correction re-prompt at sessions/2026-10-17T20-44-06-485Z_01a14b9b….jsonl:24 forced a full re-audit and re-emission of the plan (20:45:17→20:46:14); run-state.json shows planner output 7,792 tokens for a single plan; neither agents/planner.md nor agents/planner.user.md mentions JSON.
proposed_change: Add a short final paragraph: "Deliver the plan only as the JSON object the harness requires: put the complete plan markdown, escaped as a JSON string, in the `plan` field and emit nothing outside that object. Do not present the plan as prose in the final message; a response that is not a JSON object is discarded and the whole plan is regenerated."

title: Environment-installed linters are not repository gates
rationale: The implementer treated a globally installed ruff as a gate and reshaped committed code to satisfy its default rule set, even though the plan and repository standard say unconfigured static checks are recorded as not run. This added an unnecessary edit, a full re-run of its verification matrix and a review finding about code the request never asked for.
evidence: sessions/2026-10-17T20-46-14-503Z_01a14b9d….jsonl:27-30 — implementer ran `ruff --version; ruff check --isolated --show-settings`, reasoned 'ruff IS present in the environment… not a gate', then edited test_hello.py to add `check=False` plus a comment, and re-ran focused + unittest + three mutations (lines 34-36); review-1.md finding 2 exists only to discuss that `check=False`; plan.md step 3 required only checks 'already configured by the repository'; the documenter then had to explain the same line (run-state.json `results.document`).
proposed_change: In the self-review paragraph add: "Static-analysis gates come only from what the repository itself configures (its config files, CI or validation document). Tooling that merely happens to be installed in the execution environment is never a gate: you may run it to learn, but do not reshape committed code, add configuration or add comments to satisfy its defaults — record those categories as not configured, per docs/VALIDATION.md."

title: Establish the executable validation fence during the implement stage
rationale: The harness's independent validation pass executes every shell fence in docs/VALIDATION.md, but the starter validation document ships without one and only the documenter adds it — after the review loop has closed. On any repository that starts without a fence, independent verification is therefore silently skipped for every loop, and a reviewer without a shell cannot compensate.
evidence: events.jsonl:27809 `{"type":"validation_skipped","reason":"no commands in docs/VALIDATION.md"}` immediately after the implement commit; src/sf/target.py `_FENCE`/`validation_commands` read ```sh|bash|shell fences from docs/VALIDATION.md; the `## Repository Checks` fence only appears in the document stage (sessions/2026-10-17T20-49-33-161Z_01a14ba0….jsonl:22-23); review-1.md finding 1 — 'this reviewer has no shell, so AC1/AC2 could not be confirmed by executed output'.
proposed_change: In the completion-evidence paragraph add: "If the repository's validation document contains no executable shell fence covering your change, add one yourself before handing off: a fenced `sh` block of the fast, non-interactive, self-terminating commands that prove the change, with no servers, watchers or interactive commands, because the harness executes exactly those fenced commands as its independent validation and, without them, that pass is silently skipped. If the repository forbids editing that document, report the missing fence as a blocker rather than leaving it silent."

title: Plans must not contain version-control steps the implementer cannot perform
rationale: The planner wrote a commit step into the plan although the implementer is forbidden from committing and the harness commits each stage itself, so the step was dead work in the plan and in the handoff summary. The planner also spent tool calls reading repository VCS internals to infer a commit-message convention it had no use for.
evidence: plan.md step 4 'Commit the two new files in one commit following the existing message style' versus agents/implementer.md 'Do not commit; the orchestrator commits your changes'; implementer handoff (sessions/2026-10-17T20-46-14-503Z_01a14b9d….jsonl:41) 'Plan step 4 (commit): not executed — deliberately deferred'; the orchestrator made the commit (events.jsonl:27807 `sf 20261017-214405: implement (loop 1)`); planner tool calls `ls .git`, `read .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG`, `read .git/config` (sessions/2026-10-17T20-44-06-485Z_01a14b9b….jsonl:19,21,22).
proposed_change: Add to the plan-shape guidance: "Plans describe the content the implementer produces, not repository bookkeeping: the harness commits each stage and the implementer is forbidden from committing, so do not plan commit, branch, merge or message-formatting steps and do not inspect repository VCS state to infer commit conventions. State file contents and the checks that prove them."

title: A dangling document reference is drift to fix, not policy to report
rationale: The documenter correctly scanned for stale references but classed a wrong file path as a policy issue to report, so two references that point at files which do not exist in the repository remain wrong on the trunk and will keep confusing later agents; a path correction changes no requirement and belongs to the documentation stage.
evidence: run-state.json `results.document`: 'AGENTS.md §6 points to ARCHITECTURE.md in the repository root while the actual file is docs/architecture.md … left for the improvement phase'; hello1/AGENTS.md:115 still says `ARCHITECTURE.md` while the file is docs/architecture.md, and lines 8/65/164/166 still say `VALIDATION.md` while the file is docs/VALIDATION.md; the planner hit the same mismatch (sessions/2026-10-17T20-44-06-485Z_01a14b9b….jsonl:9: 'AGENTS.md references VALIDATION.md, and the inventory lists docs/VALIDATION.md').
proposed_change: Extend the drift paragraph: "A reference to a path or file name that does not exist in the repository is factual drift: repoint it at the file that actually exists, leaving the requirement it carries untouched, and list the corrected references in your summary. Reserve report-only handling for guidance whose substance would have to change."

title: Scope the formatter/linter standard to tooling this repository actually configures
rationale: The unconditional 'follow the language's standard formatter and linter' cannot be satisfied in this repository, which configures no linter, type checker or CI, so every agent has to reason around it and the implementer ended up bending code to an environment-only ruff instead of recording the category as unconfigured. Aligning the rule with docs/VALIDATION.md's 'the repository's configured linter … where applicable' removes the conflict at its source without weakening any real check.
evidence: docs/coding-standards.md final bullet 'Follow the language's standard formatter and linter.'; plan.md step 3 records 'lint, type checking, complexity and duplication gates … "Not run — not configured in this repository"'; run-state.json `results.document`: 'docs/coding-standards.md mandates a standard formatter/linter although none is configured or installed'; sessions/2026-10-17T20-46-14-503Z_01a14b9d….jsonl:27-30 shows the ruff detour this invites.
proposed_change: Replace that bullet with: 'Use the standard formatter and linter for your language when this repository configures one. This repository configures none (no linter/type-checker config, no CI): record those checks as "Not run — not configured" in your validation evidence, and never install tooling or reshape code to satisfy tools the repository has not configured.'

title: Point the improver at the run artefacts that actually exist
rationale: The task template lists `validation-*.log`, which is absent whenever validation is skipped, and does not mention that events.jsonl is dominated by duplicated streaming deltas while the real signal sits in a handful of orchestrator events and the session transcripts. Naming the artefacts and how to sample them makes the improve stage cheaper and better targeted.
evidence: this run directory contains no validation-*.log (events.jsonl:27809 `validation_skipped`), events.jsonl exceeds 34,000 lines of token deltas duplicated per event under `"source":"pi"` and `"source":"agent"`, while the decisive evidence was in run-state.json, plan.md, review-1.md and sessions/*.jsonl (tool calls and final handoff summaries).
proposed_change: Replace the run-logs bullet with: '- Run logs: {{run_dir}} — read `run-state.json`, `plan.md`, `review-*.md` and `sessions/*.jsonl` (full tool calls and handoff summaries) for substance. `events.jsonl` is mostly duplicated streaming deltas: grep it for the orchestrator events (`stage_start`, `stage_end`, `git_commit`, `agent_end`, `contract_invalid`, `validation_*`) instead of reading it, and note that `validation-*.log` exists only when validation commands ran.'
